title: Stop the lifecycle's own bookkeeping from breaking the lifecycle's own gates

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 1. Audited fc23eaa on c3fc77f/44ee98b (bookkeeping), main checkout. Sprint file read fresh. Working tree clean apart from the known .vscode file and two untracked sprint files (14, 15) that are not in this diff.

The FAIL trigger did not fire. The gate relaxation is sound and I proved it ten ways. One finding, small, on the safety argument's own wording — which this requirement specifically told me to check rather than accept.

================================================================
REQ 1 — THE LOAD-BEARING CHECK. DEMONSTRATED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, NOT READ.
================================================================

Built a scratch git repo, ran new -> start -> qa1 PASS -> dev-done, then landed a change and tried to ship.

DIRECTION 1 — bookkeeping-only must now pass. A commit containing exactly what the lifecycle writes for itself (the sprint file moved to 2-in-progress, registry.json, state/sprint-1.json) landing between audit and ship:
    "Sprint 1: shipped (commit HEAD). Phase: liveqa_live."
It ships. That is Finding A fixed, and it is the exact failure that forced a re-audit on sprint 10 and again on sprint 12.

DIRECTION 2 — everything else must still refuse. Ten separate paths, each on a fresh scratch repo, each committed between the audit and the ship attempt:
    scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py (one comment line)   REFUSED
    scripts/install.js                                REFUSED
    scripts/launcher/run-role.js                      REFUSED
    .claude/agents/qa1.md                             REFUSED
    .claude/commands/sprint-ship.md                   REFUSED
    templates/sprint-template.md                      REFUSED
    package.json (version bump)                       REFUSED
    CLAUDE.md                                         REFUSED
    a brand-new file (scripts/backdoor.js)            REFUSED
    docs/sprints/0-backlog/.gitkeep                   SHIPPED  <- see Finding 1
Nine of ten held, including a new file that did not exist at audit time. No source path slips through. Not a FAIL.

THE PRESERVED-PROTECTION CLAIM, CHECKED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED, since the requirement asks for exactly that. The comment says sprint files stay guarded by qa1_audit_file_hash in cmd_dev_done. Verified: the diff does not touch that check (qa1_audit_file_hash appears in fc23eaa only as the unchanged assignment at the PASS site), and cmd_dev_done still reads it. So the claim "this removes an overlap between two gates, not a protection" is correct for the sprint file itself. The reasoning is sound where it matters.

THE IMPLEMENTATION IS RIGHT FOR THE RIGHT REASONS. There is genuinely no git primitive for "tree minus subtree", and the ls-tree/filter/sort/sha256 approach is the correct substitute: it hashes (mode, type, blob-sha, path) per entry, sorts for determinism, and only ever needs to support equality between two calls with the same prefix — which the comment states explicitly rather than leaving someone to assume it is a real git object hash. Splitting each line on the first tab so a path containing a space cannot be mis-parsed is the kind of detail that is invisible until it bites. All three former git_tree_hash call sites were converted (cmd_qa1's PASS at 766, cmd_ship at 839, cmd_override --gate ship-hash at 1311) and none were missed — grepped rather than trusted.

================================================================
FINDING 1 (blocking, small) — "docs/sprints/ NEVER SHIPS" IS FALSE, AND SEVEN SHIPPED FILES NOW SLIP THE GATE
================================================================

git_tree_hash_excluding()'s docstring justifies the exclusion with: ".npmignore already excludes docs/sprints/ from the published tarball; what ships is the tarball's content" and, later, "docs/sprints/ never ships."

It does ship, in part. Packed the real tarball and listed it:
    package/docs/sprints/0-backlog/.gitkeep
    package/docs/sprints/1-todo/.gitkeep
    package/docs/sprints/2-in-progress/.gitkeep
    package/docs/sprints/3-done/.gitkeep
    package/docs/sprints/4-blocked/.gitkeep
    package/docs/sprints/5-abandoned/.gitkeep
    package/docs/sprints/state/.gitkeep
Seven files under docs/sprints/ are in every published package — they are the phase-folder skeleton install.js copies via SPRINT_SKELETON_FILES, and verify-tarball.sh's own output names them on every run ("clean — only .gitkeep placeholders present").

And they now slip the gate. The tenth probe above: appending a byte to docs/sprints/0-backlog/.gitkeep between audit and ship SHIPPED, where before this change it would have been refused.

PROPORTION, because I do not want this read as bigger than it is: these are empty placeholders, install.js only checks their existence and copies them, nothing reads their content, and they cannot execute. The practical exposure is that seven empty files could carry unaudited bytes into a published package. That is not a source path and it is not the FAIL trigger, which is why this is a CONDITIONAL and not a FAIL.

WHY IT IS STILL BLOCKING. This requirement's own instruction is "state the preserved protection explicitly in a comment... If that reasoning is wrong anywhere, say so and stop rather than proceeding," and its acceptance criterion tells me to check the claim rather than take the word for it. The reasoning is wrong in one clause, and that clause is load-bearing for a relaxation of this project's strongest gate. Anyone re-deriving the argument later — including whoever next widens an exclusion — inherits a premise that is not true. This project has been bitten twice this month by a claim in a comment that did not survive checking (sprint 8's exit-code call sites, sprint 12's heredoc), both times with no functional consequence and both times worth fixing.

REQUIRED FIX, and the shape is a decision, not a mechanical correction:
  EITHER narrow the exclusion so the skeleton stays covered — the shipped set is exactly the seven
  .gitkeep paths, so excluding "docs/sprints/" while keeping paths ending in ".gitkeep" is a small,
  testable change that makes the comment true as written;
  OR keep the exclusion as-is and correct the comment to say what is actually true: docs/sprints/
  ships only the seven empty phase-folder placeholders, whose content install.js never reads, and
  those are deliberately outside the ship gate.
Either is defensible. What should not survive is a gate whose stated justification does not match what it does. I have no preference between them and this is not a change I am asking to be smuggled in as a wording fix — say which one was chosen and why.

================================================================
REQ 2 — MET, AND VERIFIED AGAINST BOTH REAL RELEASES RATHER THAN THE HANDOFF
================================================================

REACHED BY READING, AS THE CRITERION DEMANDS — and I read cmd_liveqa myself rather than confirming Dev Team's reading. Its identity check is `deployed_commit != last_shipped`, resolved through git_commit_sha. gitHead appears nowhere in it. So the finding is correct: cmd_liveqa never needed gitHead, and the registry-gitHead question is a separate confidence check that LiveQA's criteria have been asking for in prose. That distinction is the right one and it is the reason this fix is not just sprint 9 again.

MECHANICAL, NOT PROSE. This is the part sprint 9 got wrong and this sprint gets right. `verify-publish` is a subcommand that reads the registry itself and logs an event, rather than an instruction telling a role to run npm view and assert what they saw. Sprint 9's version was a paragraph in pipeman.md and it drifted on the very next release; a paragraph would not have been a fix.

RAN IT AGAINST BOTH REAL RELEASES, not a sandbox:
  sprint 12 / 0.1.13 (gitHead present):
    "MATCH: registry gitHead=aa5a281960bf... == last_shipped_commit=aa5a281960bf... "
  sprint 11 / 0.1.11 (gitHead absent — the case that motivated this):
    "Registry has no gitHead recorded ... (a real, published fact, not an error here — likely a
     linked-worktree publish; falling back to content verification, which is the stronger proof
     anyway)."
    "MATCH (content): packing commit 8606700e3c5d... locally produces shasum=75e721fa9a55...,
     identical to the registry's dist.shasum for fully-completely@0.1.11."
The fallback is the better half. gitHead is a self-reported label; dist.shasum against a locally reproduced pack is the published bytes themselves. Calling that "the stronger proof anyway" in the output is accurate, not a consolation, and recording gitHead's absence as a stated fact rather than an error is the right handling of a thing that is genuinely absent.

================================================================
REQS 3, 4, 5 — MET
================================================================

Req 3 — warns, never gates, confirmed by construction: worktree_divergence_warning() has no die() and no exit on any path; every failure mode returns None and every success returns a string. Checked for the ruled-out approach too: `origin/` appears nowhere in executable code, only in a comment explaining why it was rejected — which is sprint 7's reasoning correctly carried rather than rediscovered.

Req 4 — package.json is 0.1.14, one line, and 0.1.13 was confirmed live first.

Req 5 — ran it: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED. verify-tarball.sh: TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED, "Installed 0.1.14 (first install)".

CODE QUALITY

Error handling: every new subprocess path collapses to None the same way the existing git helpers do, with the reason stated rather than assumed.
Standards: the exclusion prefix is a named module constant with a comment explaining it is a git-tree path and not a filesystem path — a distinction that would otherwise be discovered the hard way on Windows. Malformed ls-tree lines are skipped rather than crashing.
Security: this is a gate relaxation, which is the highest-risk category this project has, and it was verified in both directions against a real scratch repo rather than by reading. The relaxation is correctly scoped everywhere except the seven files in Finding 1.

RECOMMENDATION

One decision and one edit. Then round 2 is short — I have no other open items, and I will be re-running the same ten probes plus whichever direction you pick.

Then /sprint-dev-done 13 and ship. Worth noting the irony deliberately: this sprint is the one that makes shipping-after-bookkeeping work, and it will be the first release able to ship without tripping the gate it fixes.

PASS: PASS — round 2. Audited e575d21 with bookkeeping 0a08adb, main checkout. Sprint file re-read fresh; `git diff fc23eaa HEAD -- docs/sprints/2-in-progress/` is empty, so the requirements are byte-identical to round 1's. Working tree clean apart from the known .vscode file and two untracked sprint files (14, 15) not in this diff.

The finding is closed, and I re-ran every probe rather than checking the one that changed.

================================================================
THE FIX — NARROWING, AND IT HOLDS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS
================================================================

SHIP_HASH_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS is now four fnmatch globs rather than a directory prefix:
    docs/sprints/.locks/*
    docs/sprints/registry.json
    docs/sprints/state/*.json
    docs/sprints/*/*.md
That mirrors what actually ships versus what the lifecycle writes, which is the distinction the round-1 comment claimed and did not have. Nothing under docs/sprints/ that appears in the tarball matches any of these — .gitkeep is not .json and not .md — so the seven shipped placeholders are back inside the gate.

RE-RAN ALL TEN ROUND-1 PROBES, PLUS BOTH .gitkeep CASES, each on a fresh scratch repo, each committed between the audit and the ship attempt:
    scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py            REFUSED
    scripts/install.js                     REFUSED
    scripts/launcher/run-role.js           REFUSED
    .claude/agents/qa1.md                  REFUSED
    .claude/commands/sprint-ship.md        REFUSED
    templates/sprint-template.md           REFUSED
    package.json                           REFUSED
    CLAUDE.md                              REFUSED
    a brand-new scripts/backdoor.js        REFUSED
    docs/sprints/0-backlog/.gitkeep        REFUSED   <- was SHIPPED in round 1; the finding, closed
    docs/sprints/state/.gitkeep            REFUSED   <- checked too, since state/*.json wouldn't catch it
Eleven for eleven. The round-1 hole is shut and nothing else moved.

DIRECTION 1 STILL WORKS, which is the half a narrowing could plausibly have broken. A commit containing the full set of lifecycle bookkeeping — sprint file moved into 2-in-progress, registry.json, state/sprint-1.json — still ships: "Sprint 1: shipped (commit HEAD). Phase: liveqa_live." Finding A remains fixed.

AND THE .locks CASE, VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY. Built a scratch repo where a real run had left lock files in the tree, committed them with the rest of the bookkeeping after the audit, and shipped: two .locks entries in the commit, still ships. That is the miss Dev Team's own new test caught before commit, and it holds under my construction of it too rather than only under theirs.

CREDIT WHERE IT IS DUE, because it is the point of having tests at all: the first narrowed list was incomplete in exactly the way a hand-copied list gets incomplete — .locks/ sits in .npmignore grouped with unrelated OS and Python cruft rather than in the three-line block that was copied. The regression test written this round caught it immediately, from a real lock file produced by a real bookkeeping run, before it reached a commit. That is a test doing the job a test exists for, and reporting both the miss and the catch in the commit message rather than only the fix is the right way to hand it over. I would not have caught it — my round-1 probes never produced a lock file, because I never ran two lifecycle commands concurrently.

================================================================
SCOPE, AND EVERYTHING ELSE STANDS
================================================================

Round-2 diff is scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py (111 lines, the pattern list plus its matching and comments), scripts/smoke_test.sh (32 lines, the new regression tests), and three state files — two of which are my own round-1 verify-publish runs being committed. No requirement, no other source file.

Not re-derived, verified in round 1 and unchanged: cmd_dev_done's qa1_audit_file_hash check untouched; all three former git_tree_hash call sites converted with none missed; Req 2's verify-publish reaching the right answer against both real releases (0.1.13 gitHead match, 0.1.11 content fallback against the registry's own dist.shasum); Req 3 warning without ever gating and introducing no origin/* comparison.

Re-ran everything anyway: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, ALL WORKTREE TESTS PASSED, ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED (123 OK). verify-tarball.sh: "Installed 0.1.14 (first install)", TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED. package.json 0.1.14.

================================================================
INFORMATIONAL — NOT REQUIRED FIXES
================================================================

1. VERIFY-PUBLISH WRITES TO CLOSED SPRINTS, and my own audit is the evidence. Running `verify-publish 11` and `verify-publish 12` in round 1 appended content_check and gitHead-match events to both sprints' history — and both are phase=complete, closed on 2026-09-03. Those writes are in this round's commit.
   I am not calling it a defect: the events are append-only, the actor is clearly labelled "verify-publish", nothing either gate reads was touched, and recording that a published release was verified is a fact worth having. But "closed" now does not mean "immutable," and that should be a deliberate choice rather than a side effect nobody named. If it is intended, one line in the command's docstring saying so is enough. If it is not, the fix is to refuse on a completed sprint. Worth deciding before an automated caller runs it in a loop.

2. THE SMOKE COUNT IS NOT VERIFIABLE AS STATED. The handoff says "122/122 smoke tests (stable across three runs)". The suite prints no total — it emits 50 `== ` section headers, no per-test ok lines, and ends with "ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED", aborting on the first failure. The obvious internal counts are 148 `|| fail`/`&& fail` guards and 169 total `fail` invocations. None of those is 122, and I cannot tell what was being counted.
   I am recording this as unverifiable rather than as a miscount, because unlike launcher_test.js this suite gives no self-reported number to check against, and I would rather be accurate about the limits of my own check than score a point. No verdict impact — the suite passes, which is what the criterion asked for. If a count is going to be quoted, the suite should print one; that is a cheaper fix than remembering to derive it by hand.

3. Carried, unchanged: the --agents argv budget against Windows' 32,767-char limit, and the interactive auth-check ordering from sprint 11 round 1.

================================================================
RECOMMENDATION
================================================================

Ship it. /sprint-dev-done 13, then Pipeman ships e575d21 or the bookkeeping commit on top — and this is the first sprint where that sentence is not a trap. The gate this sprint fixes is the one that has forced a re-audit on sprints 10 and 12 for bookkeeping that was never a risk, and it now distinguishes what ships from what the lifecycle writes about itself.

Then run `verify-publish 13` after the publish rather than asserting gitHead by hand. That is the whole point of Req 2, and this release is its first real use.

PASS: PASS — round 1. Live-tested published npm 0.1.14 by driving four real sprints through the real gates from a published install. Environment: macOS Darwin arm64, scratch git repo /tmp/fc14 plus a real linked worktree at /tmp/fc14-devteam2-sprint-4, 2026-09-04.

No billed agent runs were needed this round — every criterion here is a lifecycle-script property, so all of it was exercised directly and cheaply.

PROVENANCE — VERIFIED BY HAND FIRST, THEN THE NEW TOOL WAS TESTED AGAINST IT
`npm view fully-completely version` -> 0.1.14; `npm view fully-completely@0.1.14 gitHead` -> e575d2133251b558fe492ef5af86df7a64be23b8, an exact match for last_shipped_commit. Remote tag v0.1.14 dereferences to the same commit.

FIRST ATTEMPT, NO CORRECTION — which is this criterion's actual test. Sprint 13's history contains a single `pipeman shipped commit=e575d21` event and NO `reshipped` event. Sprints 6, 8 and 9 all needed a post-hoc correction; this one did not, and neither did 10 through 12. Req 2 works.

I deliberately did my own `npm view` check before looking at what verify-publish recorded, so the tool was compared against an independent result rather than believed.

A NOTE ON A FIELD THAT CHANGED SHAPE. qa1_audited_tree_hash for sprint 13 is 64 hex characters, where every prior sprint's was 40. That is not corruption: sprint 13 replaced the raw git tree hash with `git_tree_hash_excluding()`, a sha256 over the tree with bookkeeping paths filtered out. I chased it before scoring because a malformed hash in that field is exactly what would silently break `/sprint-ship`'s content check, and a 40-to-64 character change is what corruption would look like too. It is the intended design.

================================================================
CRITERION 1 — 0.1.14 ON THE REGISTRY, gitHead MATCHING, NO CORRECTION: PASS. Covered above.
================================================================

================================================================
CRITERION 2 — A REAL SPRINT THROUGH THE REAL GATES WITH BOOKKEEPING LANDING MID-FLIGHT: PASS
================================================================
The criterion is explicit that a sprint with no bookkeeping proves nothing, so both runs had real bookkeeping commits landing between the audit and the ship.

Run A — ship the audited commit while HEAD has moved past it:
  built a real source change (src/app.js), committed  -> audited commit d33b66c
  /sprint-qa1 1 --verdict PASS
  committed "BOOKKEEPING: qa1 PASS recorded"
  /sprint-dev-done 1
  committed "BOOKKEEPING: dev-done"
  HEAD now 2 bookkeeping commits past the audit
  /sprint-ship 1 --commit d33b66c  ->  "Sprint 1: shipped. Phase: liveqa_live."  ACCEPTED

Run B — the harder and more realistic case, ship HEAD ITSELF when HEAD contains bookkeeping the audit never saw:
  same shape, audited a source build, then two bookkeeping commits on top
  /sprint-ship 2 --commit HEAD  ->  "Sprint 2: shipped. Phase: liveqa_live."  ACCEPTED

Before sprint 13 this is the case that failed: the lifecycle's own state writes changed the tree, so the tree-hash gate rejected a commit whose source was byte-identical to what QA1 audited. Pipeman's own releases repeatedly hit it. Both runs now pass, which is the sprint's central claim demonstrated on shipped code.

================================================================
CRITERION 3 — THE RELAXATION DID NOT OPEN A HOLE: PASS. THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED.
================================================================
Same setup, but with a genuine unaudited source change smuggled in after the PASS:
  built src/app3.js ("audited version"), committed, /sprint-qa1 3 --verdict PASS, bookkeeping commit, /sprint-dev-done 3
  then overwrote src/app3.js with "UNAUDITED SNEAKY CHANGE" and committed it
  /sprint-ship 3 --commit HEAD

  ERROR: Sprint 3: the commit being shipped doesn't match what QA1 audited (its file contents
  differ, even accounting for a rebase/squash/merge that preserves content). New changes landed
  after QA1's PASS need a fresh /sprint-qa1 audit before they can ship. No override.

So the exclusion is scoped to bookkeeping paths only. A one-line change to real source, in a sprint whose bookkeeping churn was otherwise identical to the two runs that shipped, is still refused with no override. The relaxation loosened exactly what it claimed to loosen and nothing else — verified by the pair, not by reading the exclusion list.

================================================================
CRITERION 4 — THE WORKTREE WARNING FIRES: PASS
================================================================
Created a real Dev Team 2 worktree with the shipped `scripts/dev2_worktree.sh 4` (branch devteam2/sprint-4, at /private/tmp/fc14-devteam2-sprint-4), amended the sprint file inside the worktree and committed it there, then ran a command from the main tree, which now holds the stale copy. Verbatim:

  WARNING: sprint 4's file differs from the copy in 1 other worktree:
  /private/tmp/fc14-devteam2-sprint-4. This read is from /private/tmp/fc14 only — if another
  session amended the sprint file elsewhere, this may be a stale copy. Not gated: worktrees are
  exactly how this framework expects roles to work in parallel, this only makes the divergence
  visible rather than silent.

It names the diverging worktree by path, names which tree the read came from, and states plainly that it is not a gate. This is the scenario that had Dev Team building against a stale spec, and a reader now has both facts needed to diagnose it. Read cold, it does not read as an error, which is correct — it is not one.

================================================================
verify-publish ITSELF — TESTED FOR ITS NEGATIVE CASE, NOT JUST ITS HAPPY PATH
================================================================
This command now performs the check I have done by hand at every gate since sprint 3, so the thing worth establishing is not that it can say MATCH but that it can say NO. A verifier that always agrees is worse than no verifier, because it retires the manual check that was working.

Forced a real mismatch in the scratch repo, where nothing is at stake: sprint 2's last_shipped_commit is 8d0e497e44d25be032e2d3a76f587057b88949f6, which is not what npm published for 0.1.14.

  MISMATCH: registry gitHead=e575d213... != last_shipped_commit=8d0e497e... for fully-completely@0.1.14.

and it recorded that negative result to the state file as a `gitHead_check` event rather than only logging successes. It can say no, and it writes down when it does.

Its refusals are also clean rather than silent. With no package.json present: "Could not read a package name from package.json, and none was given via --package. Pass --package explicitly." With no resolvable version: the equivalent message naming --version. Both name the remedy; neither guesses.

I did not run it against sprint 13 in the real repository. Pipeman already did, and its result is on the record there; running it again would append a duplicate event for no gain, and I had already established the same fact independently by hand.

================================================================
ISSUE 1 — LOW/MEDIUM, DESIGN QUESTION, ALREADY QA1's — CONFIRMED LIVE IN THE SHIPPED RELEASE
================================================================
verify-publish writes to CLOSED sprints. Confirmed in this repository's own state files:
  sprint 11  phase=complete  2 verify-publish events (content_check, 23:14:00 and 23:24:52)
  sprint 12  phase=complete  2 verify-publish events (gitHead_check, 23:13:50 and 23:24:29)
Both sprints were closed before those events were appended, and both appear in the shipped commit range.

I nearly missed this and want the method on the record: my first sweep grepped the `event` field for "verify" and returned zero, because the events are named `content_check`/`gitHead_check` and only the `actor` field says verify-publish. The clean result was an artifact of my query, not of the data. Re-run against `actor`, it is plainly there.

Not a gate problem: the writes are append-only and touch none of the five fields either gate reads, so nothing can be laundered and no verdict is affected. It is a records-integrity question — whether a completed sprint's history is immutable — and QA1 is right that it deserves a deliberate answer rather than an implicit one. Master Controller's call, not a fix I am demanding, and it does not affect this verdict.

================================================================
ISSUE 2 — LOW, COSMETIC, THE PROJECT'S OWN FAVOURITE DEFECT CLASS
================================================================
`/sprint-ship`'s printed confirmation echoes the raw `--commit` argument instead of what it stored:
  ship 1 --commit d33b66c  ->  "Sprint 1: shipped (commit d33b66c249f3cae7076606e4fced3fc9a08dfb72)."
  ship 2 --commit HEAD     ->  "Sprint 2: shipped (commit HEAD)."
The stored value is correct in both cases — I checked the state file, and sprint 2 holds the resolved 8d0e497e..., not the literal string. So this is display only and nothing downstream is wrong.

Recording it because it is precisely the class this project keeps catching: a message that does not say what actually happened. Anyone shipping with `--commit HEAD` cannot tell from the output which commit was recorded, which is the fact LiveQA's `--deployed-commit` must later match exactly. One line, whenever that function is next touched.

================================================================
WHAT I OBSERVED VS ACCEPTED
================================================================
Every result above I produced by running the shipped 0.1.14 in a scratch git repository with a real linked worktree. Provenance was established by my own `npm view` before I looked at verify-publish's recorded result, and verify-publish was then tested for its failure mode rather than accepted on its successes. Pipeman's claims about gitHead and about verify-publish's fallback were both checked. QA1's two passed-along notes were checked rather than relayed: the closed-sprint writes are confirmed present in this repo's own state files; the smoke-test count question I did not investigate, as it is a static property and QA1 has already correctly marked it unverifiable rather than wrong.

================================================================
RECOMMENDATION
================================================================
Ship-ready. All four criteria pass with evidence, and the pair that matters most — bookkeeping-only churn ships, a one-line source change does not — was demonstrated as a controlled pair rather than inferred from the exclusion list. The gate this sprint relaxed is now looser in exactly one dimension and no looser anywhere else, and the new verify-publish command can produce a negative verdict and records it when it does.

Two items carry forward, neither blocking: whether a closed sprint's history should be immutable (QA1's question, now confirmed live), and the ship message that echoes its argument rather than its result.

This PASS means the code is ready, not that anyone is authorized to close sprint 13.
